route: Slovakia has no residence permit for people of independent means. The Act on the Residence of Foreigners (404/2011) lists temporary-residence purposes in par. 22 (business), 23 (employment), 24 (study), 25 (special activity: lecturing, art, sport, internship, government programmes, treaty duties, health care, volunteering, accredited journalist), 26 (research), 27 (family reunification) and 30 (long-term resident from another member state). None fits a 45-year-old couple living on investments. Family reunification with a Slovak or resident spouse, or a business permit (par. 22), are the nearest. Whatever the purpose, par. 123 of the Act defines the required proof: 'Dokladom potvrdzujucim zdravotne poistenie sa rozumie potvrdenie na meno cudzinca o tom, ze je zdravotne poisteny na uzemi Slovenskej republiky alebo ze ma poistenu uhradu liecebnych nakladov na uzemi Slovenskej republiky.' Par. 32(9): a foreigner under par. 22, 25, 26, 27 and 30 must hand over the proof of health insurance within 30 days of receiving the residence document.
policy: Public insurance is not open to them while on temporary residence: Act 580/2004 par. 3(2) makes a person 'verejne zdravotne poistena' if she 'ma trvaly pobyt na uzemi Slovenskej republiky'; par. 3(3) extends this to non-permanent-residents only if employed in Slovakia, self-employed with a permit, certain students and similar groups. So a non-working, non-EU couple needs commercial cover. The mainstream product found is Union's 'Zdravotne poistenie cudzincov SAFETY' (Dovera refers its customers to it with a discount): cover for emergency care up to EUR 70,000 and repatriation up to EUR 20,000 on the cheaper tier; SAFETY adds comprehensive care, including outpatient and inpatient care and prescribed medicines. Union and Dovera publish no premium; Union's calculator was not used.
working: No premium published, so no sum. A figure would need a calculator quote, which means entering a name, date of birth and often an email, which the brief forbids.

income_based_charges.name: Slovak public health insurance for a person with permanent residence and no employment or self-employment (par. 11(2))
income_based_charges.rate: 15% of the assessment base (par. 12(1)(e)); the law text also shows a 16% rate in a later-effective amendment, not resolved
income_based_charges.base: Actual income, subject to a minimum base of 50% of the average monthly wage (par. 13(10)); the average wage figure was not retrieved
income_based_charges.includes_capital_gains: unclear: not read; par. 13 covers dividends separately (par. 13(14)) and caps dividend income at 60 times the average monthly wage
income_based_charges.floor: 50% of the average monthly wage x 15%; euro amount not computed because the wage figure was not fetched

eu_citizen_difference: An EU citizen living in Slovakia and registered as a Union citizen under par. 65 of Act 404/2011 must show 'doklad o zdravotnom poisteni' and sufficient means, but is not tied to a purpose-of-stay permit. EU citizens employed in Slovakia join the public system on day one.
spot_check: None possible: no premium was reachable.
uncertainty: No sourced premium: amount is null. The legal requirement is only 'insurance that covers treatment costs in Slovakia', with no stated minimum limit, so even a cheap EUR 70,000 policy may satisfy it. After permanent residence (usually 5 years) the couple would enter public insurance and pay 15% of income with a minimum base of 50% of the average wage; the euro figure was not computed. The route itself is the bigger doubt: no permit fits this couple.
